slides.heading: Remove Duplicates From Linked List
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Remove Duplicates From Linked List, an easy linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: List is sorted; remove nodes with repeated values in place.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. List is sorted; remove nodes with repeated values in place.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: The list is sorted, so duplicates are adjacent; we can skip them in place.
slides.narration: The list is sorted, so duplicates are adjacent; we can skip them in place.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: With a hash set: works for unsorted lists, O(n) space
Sorted list: duplicates are adjacent → O(1) space
slides.narration: A hash set would work even for unsorted lists, but costs extra space. Because this list is sorted, duplicates are always adjacent, so we can just skip over them in place.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. While the next node has the same value, bypass it
3. Move to the next distinct node
slides.narration: Step by step. First, walk the list. Second, while the next node has the same value, bypass it. Third, move to the next distinct node. Fourth, return the head.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each node, we find the next node with a different value, point current dot next at it, and move current forward.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Runs of 3+ duplicates (loop, don't just skip one)
slides.narration: Handle long runs of duplicates with an inner loop, not a single skip, and make sure the end of the list works.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: remove ALL nodes that had duplicates
slides.narration: A tricky follow-up removes every value that had duplicates entirely. For unsorted lists, use a hash set.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: The list is sorted, so duplicates are adjacent; we can skip them in place.
